title: Number classifier
brief: Find the numbers in the input and print each on its own line with its kind. HEX is 0x or 0X followed by hex digits. FLOAT is digits with a fraction, an exponent or both, as in 3.14, 2.5e3 or 1e5. INT is plain digits. Ignore everything else.

tests.name: A leading zero is still INT
A lone dot is not a fraction

hints: Named definitions keep this readable. Put DIGIT [0-9] in the first section and write {DIGIT}+ in the rules.
An exponent is [eE][-+]?{DIGIT}+. Make it optional when there is a fraction, and required when there is not.
Longest match separates them: 3.14 could start as INT 3, but FLOAT takes more characters, so FLOAT wins.
explanation: Each kind gets its own rule, and longest match picks the right one. On 0x1F the INT rule only reaches 0, while HEX reaches the end. A lone dot never starts a number, so .5 is an ignored dot followed by INT 5.
